headline: Every living thing is made of cells—the smallest units that are fully alive
universal_truth: Life organizes itself into units that contain everything needed to function
fun_facts: Your body contains about 37 trillion cells—more than stars in the Milky Way
Some organisms are just one cell; you were once a single cell too
Cells are so small that 10,000 could fit on the head of a pin
discussion_questions: What makes something 'alive' versus just a complex machine?
How does knowing you have 37 trillion cells change your sense of self?
What does it mean that you started as a single cell?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You are not one thing. You are 37 trillion things—37 trillion cells working together. Each cell is a complete living unit: it eats, produces waste, responds to its environment, and can reproduce. You are a city of cells, cooperating.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Where did cells come from? The first cells appeared over 3.5 billion years ago. But what makes a cell alive? What does a cell have that non-living chemistry lacks?

options.text: Cells contain DNA instructions, metabolism, and a membrane that separates inside from outside
options.response: Yes. A cell has information, energy processing, and boundaries—the minimal requirements for life.

options.text: Cells have a special life force that chemistry alone cannot create
options.response: Cells are remarkable, but they follow physical laws...

q1.title: Cities of Cells
q1.script: Your 37 trillion cells include about 200 different types—nerve cells, blood cells, skin cells, muscle cells. Each type is specialized. Like a city has doctors, builders, and garbage collectors, your body has cells for every function.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Cities of Cells"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Self-Contained Units
q2.script: Each cell contains everything needed for life: DNA with instructions, ribosomes to build proteins, mitochondria for energy, and a membrane to maintain boundaries. A cell is the smallest thing that can do everything life requires.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: From One to Trillions
q3.script: You started as one cell—a fertilized egg. That single cell divided, then divided again. Those cells specialized and organized. In nine months, one cell became the trillions that compose you. Your whole body is one cell's descendants.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You are a community. The cells remind us that what seems like 'one' is actually many working together. Your identity emerges from trillions of living units cooperating. Individuality is collective.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 78. Tomorrow, we'll discover your body's instruction manual—DNA. Until then, appreciate the 37 trillion cells that make 'you' possible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Cellular Self - You Are a Community
growTrack.learning_objective: See yourself as a cooperative system, not a single unit
growTrack.activity: Consider that 'you' are 37 trillion cells cooperating. What does this mean for self-care? Taking care of yourself means taking care of a vast community. What does your cellular community need today—rest, fuel, movement, repair?
